findings.title: Workflow reminder cancellation is not awaited
findings.body: The new calls to deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...) are made inside a synchronous forEach with no promise collected or awaited. deleteScheduledEmailReminder now performs async work (Prisma update/delete, and sometimes a SendGrid request), so the cancellation endpoint can return before that work finishes; on serverless runtimes the pending work may be terminated entirely. The same fire-and-forget pattern exists in handleNewBooking.ts around line 968, bookings.tsx around line 490, and workflows.tsx around lines 214/378/521/576. Consequence: a cancelled or rescheduled booking can leave its reminder active, so the workflow email is still sent, which is exactly the failure this PR is meant to fix.

findings.title: One SendGrid cancellation error blocks all other cancellations
findings.body: The entire cancellation loop is covered by one try/catch. If client.request fails for one reminder, execution jumps to the catch, so no later reminder in remindersToCancel is processed, and the Prisma delete promises already collected in workflowRemindersToDelete are never awaited. A single stale or failed batch_id can therefore leave many cancelled reminders active and allow their emails to be sent; successfully cancelled rows also remain in the database. Cancellations should be handled per reminder (or with allSettled), and rows should be deleted only after their own cancellation succeeds.

findings.title: Cron window does not guarantee cancellation for imminent reminders
findings.body: The cron only picks up cancelled reminders whose scheduledDate is at or before now + 1 hour, but the job runs every 15 minutes. A reminder cancelled just after a cron run and due in, say, 5-10 minutes will not be visited until the next cron run, after SendGrid has already sent the email. The one-hour lookahead does not fix near-term cancellations by itself; imminent reminders need immediate cancellation or a processing mechanism that can run before their send time.

findings.title: Immediate cancellation path has no retry or DB cleanup
findings.body: When immediateDelete is true, deleteScheduledEmailReminder sends the SendGrid cancel request and returns without setting cancelled = true or deleting the WorkflowReminder row. Errors are caught and only logged. handleNewBooking uses this immediate path when a booking is rescheduled, so a transient SendGrid/network failure leaves the old reminder scheduled with no cron retry, and even on success the old row remains scheduled in the database. A failed immediate cancellation should fall back to marking the reminder cancelled (or otherwise be retried), and successful cancellations should clean up the row where the caller does not cascade-delete it.

findings.title: No test coverage for new cancellation lifecycle
findings.body: No tests were added for the new cancelled flag, the cron cancellation/deletion flow, or the reschedule cancellation path. The previous implementation was wrong without being caught, so regressions here will silently send workflow emails again. Coverage should include: marking a reminder cancelled, the cron cancelling and deleting it, SendGrid failure behavior, reminders without referenceId, and rescheduled bookings cancelling old reminders.
